extracted.intended_audience: scholars, students, and practitioners in journalism, communication studies, media analysis, and news editors/modelers
extracted.subtask_description: A theory-driven framework for evaluating how newsroom selection and framing of political news 'index' the range of viewpoints expressed by mainstream government elites; useful for analyzing newsworthiness, source inclusion, and homepage story framing. Applies to empirical tests (e.g., measuring viewpoint diversity against elite debate) and operational decisions in news production.

rubrics_metrics.name: Indexing Hypothesis (core claim)
rubrics_metrics.description: "Mass media news professionals, from the boardroom to the beat reporter, tend to 'index' the range of voices and viewpoints in both news and editorials according to the range of views expressed in mainstream government debate about a given topic."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is the central evaluative standard: coverage should be judged by how well the set of voices presented maps onto the set of views present in elite government debate. Use as a baseline expectation for political-issue coverage; deviations from indexing are notable and require explanation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Elite Consensus → News Consensus
rubrics_metrics.description: When the White House and congressional leaders agree, news coverage will reflect that consensus, ignoring dissenting voices.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Predicts narrow, largely uncritical coverage when major government elites share a position; use as a diagnostic for why critical perspectives may be absent despite public disagreement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Elite Disagreement → News Coverage of Both Sides
rubrics_metrics.description: When elites split, news coverage will fall within the range of their disagreement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Expect coverage to broaden to include the range of elite viewpoints; measure whether reported perspectives correspond to the poles of elite debate rather than to non-elite or public opinion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public Opinion Outside Elite Range Exclusion
rubrics_metrics.description: Public opinion outside the range of elite debate is largely excluded; even when polls show majority support for a position, if no major elite voice supports it, news will not represent it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat absence of widely held public views in coverage as consistent with indexing unless an elite source articulates those views; contrasts public-opinion metrics with elite-source representation to evaluate coverage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Source Authorization Threshold
rubrics_metrics.description: For a viewpoint to be reportable, an authorized elite source must articulate it. No elite voice → no representation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Operational criterion for source selection: journalists tend to require an 'authorized' elite actor before including a viewpoint. Use this to evaluate why particular perspectives were omitted or included.

rubrics_metrics.name: Indexed Diversity (bounded perspective breadth)
rubrics_metrics.description: The breadth of perspectives in news coverage is bounded above by the breadth of elite debate, not by the breadth of public opinion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Quantify diversity in coverage against diversity of elite-source viewpoints; if coverage shows greater diversity than elite debate, it is a deviation from the hypothesis and warrants scrutiny.

rubrics_metrics.name: Critical-Story Restriction
rubrics_metrics.description: Critical stories about government policy are gated by whether elites are willing to criticize. Bipartisan elite consensus shields policy from media scrutiny.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When elites present bipartisan support, expect fewer investigative/critical stories; evaluate whether critical reporting appears only after elite fissures emerge.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evidentiary Asymmetry
rubrics_metrics.description: Reports challenging elite consensus must clear higher evidentiary bars than reports affirming it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess editorial evidentiary standards asymmetrically: accusations or challenges to established elite positions will face stricter sourcing and proof requirements than confirmatory reports.

rubrics_metrics.name: Beat-Channel Capture
rubrics_metrics.description: Beats organized around official institutions (White House, Congress, Pentagon) systematically reproduce institutional perspectives.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use beat-structure analysis to predict source flows: institutional beats will favor official/elite frames; enterprise reporting is required to surface non-elite perspectives.

rubrics_metrics.name: Objectivity Rituals as Gatekeeping
rubrics_metrics.description: Objectivity rituals require authoritative sources; only elites are reliably authoritative (Tuchman 1972).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Understand newsroom norms (e.g., 'balance', reliance on official sources) as institutional pressures that privilege elite voices; evaluate whether invocation of 'objectivity' served to exclude non-elite viewpoints.

rubrics_metrics.name: Routine Channels (institutional sourcing)
rubrics_metrics.description: Reporters work official-institutional beats; elite voices flow naturally; non-elite voices require enterprise (Sigal 1973).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examine reporting routines: reliance on routine channels makes inclusion of non-elite perspectives less likely unless reporters pursue enterprise reporting or have elite allies to legitimize those voices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Risk Mitigation (political/reputational risk)
rubrics_metrics.description: Stories outside the indexed range expose outlets to political and reputational risk.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider organizational incentives: avoidance of politically risky framings reduces likelihood of covering out-of-range viewpoints; use this to explain conservative selection tendencies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pack Convergence
rubrics_metrics.description: Reporters check what other reporters cover; this reassures story selection and reproduces the indexed range across outlets (Donsbach 2004).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess inter-outlet convergence as a reinforcing mechanism: if multiple outlets follow elite cues, the same limited range of views will dominate the news ecosystem.

rubrics_metrics.name: Empirical phase-pattern in crisis/war coverage
rubrics_metrics.description: In wars and crises, elite consensus typically forms initially → narrow critical coverage in early phases; as elites split, coverage broadens.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use phase-based analysis (e.g., Bennett's contra-war phases) to predict when coverage will shift from consensus to more contested framing; useful for temporal modeling of homepage story selection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quantitative test: measure coverage vs. elite viewpoints
rubrics_metrics.description: For any political issue, the diversity of viewpoints in news coverage can be measured against the diversity of elite-source viewpoints; deviation from indexing should be small.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Operationalizable metric for researchers and homepage modelers: code story framings and elite-source positions, compute overlap or divergence, and treat large deviations as noteworthy anomalies requiring explanation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Protest Breakthrough Condition (elite ally mediation)
rubrics_metrics.description: Only protest viewpoints articulated by an elite ally enter mainstream coverage (per Gitlin 1980).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When evaluating whether activist or protest voices appear in coverage, check for articulation or endorsement by elite actors as the likely mechanism enabling mainstream inclusion.
